sentence: This project studies how proteins that assemble themselves work in the innate immune system and may explain the chronic inflammation of aging.
This project builds radiotracers for imaging two proteins, alpha-synuclein and tau, in diseases such as Parkinson's disease and frontotemporal dementia.
This project studies aggressive prostate cancer, including why it resists treatments, and looks for biomarkers to tailor treatment for patients.
This project gives vision researchers equipment and advice for measuring RNA, DNA and proteins in tissue samples and in genetically modified mice.
This project tries to find out which molecular and cellular changes cause memory impairment in temporal lobe epilepsy.
This project builds chemical tools that find and block lysyl oxidase enzymes, to learn what these enzymes do in cancer.
This project studies early Alzheimer disease and related dementias in Black and White adults in their sixties, and how it differs by race and sex.
This project tries to find out how certain neutrophils keep the immune system suppressed in glioblastoma brain tumors.
This project builds trophoblast organoids from human stem cells to model preeclampsia and test drugs.
This project uses simulation to study how simple interactions lead to complex behavior in proteins, ribosomes and the spread of viral diseases.
This project studies how an HIV protein interacts with a human protein complex and why this matters for infection.
This project builds sensors that reveal the local lipids around membrane proteins in living mammalian cells.
This project studies how interferon gamma signaling affects tumor growth and immune suppression in neuroendocrine prostate cancer after hormone therapy failure.
This project builds fiber probes that combine mid-infrared photothermal imaging and fluorescence imaging to find tissue abnormalities and tumors.
This project monitors immune and genomic changes in the blood and tumor of patients with ovarian cancer who receive immunotherapies.
This project studies how advanced glycation end products change prostate tumor biology in different populations.
This project looks for genetic causes of autosomal dominant polycystic kidney disease and uses cells and whole animals to test gene variants.
This project tries to find out how the immune system attacks saliva producing glands in Sjögren disease.
This project studies how changes in DNA and epigenetics, and control of transcription, are linked to cancer.
